title: Optimal Selection and Placement of Voltage Regulators in 2.5D Heterogeneously Integrated Systems
problem: 2.5D heterogeneously integrated systems require optimal voltage regulator (VR) placement for efficient power delivery with heterogeneous chiplet loads and nonuniform power distributions.
motivation: Manual VR placement becomes intractable as systems scale; automation is essential for meeting power delivery specifications across diverse chiplet configurations.
method: Formulates VR selection and placement as 0–1 MILP using macromodeling to manage problem size, optimizing for number, location, and type of switched-capacitor voltage regulators (SCVRs) on active silicon interposer.
key_novelty: Automated MILP-based optimization for heterogeneous VR placement in 2.5D systems using macromodeling for scalability.
limitations: Tested on four cases; applicability to larger, more complex systems and dynamic power profiles unclear.
primary_theme: MILP-based VR optimization for 2.5D heterogeneous systems
